products.name: furcula
products.description: The furcula bone is found among birds and some dinosaurs, and is commonly referred to as the wishbone. It is formed by the fusion of two clavicles and serves to strengthen the thoracic skeleton to withstand the rigors of flight.

products.name: foramen
products.description: A foramen is a hole in a bone that allows for the passage of nerves and blood vessels.

products.name: Disc
products.description: A disc is a flat, circular structure that can be found in various parts of the body, such as the spine. It serves as a cushion between bones and helps to absorb shock and maintain flexibility.

products.name: Marrow
products.description: The marrow is the soft, fatty tissue found inside bones. It plays a crucial role in producing blood cells.

products.name: suture
products.description: A suture is a fibrous joint between two bones of the skull, where the bones are united by a thin layer of fibrous connective tissue.

products.name: cartilage
products.description: Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue that serves as a cushion between bones and allows for smooth joint movement.

products.name: rib-cage
products.description: The rib cage is a bony structure that protects the heart and lungs.

products.name: joint
products.description: A joint is a connection between two bones that allows for movement and flexibility.

products.name: omoplates
products.description: Shoulder blades, also known as omoplates or scapulae, are flat, triangular bones located on the upper back. They connect the humerus (upper arm bone) with the clavicle (collarbone) and provide attachment points for various muscles that facilitate shoulder and arm movements.

products.name: jaw
products.description: The jawbone, also known as the mandible, is the largest and strongest bone in the human face.
